set.body:
Phase C (P0, isolated to kernel).

The review's own correction is upheld: writeStable ALREADY takes the sidecar lock (kernel/AtomicFiles.scala:75), not just publishOnce (:107). The remaining holes are real:

- writeNewBlocking (:52) does an unlocked Files.exists then stageAndMove.
- claimBlocking (:133) does an unlocked Files.exists(to) then Files.move.

So the kernel has two locked operations and two unlocked ones against the same class of destination race, and the class doc at :96-101 explains precisely why the lock is necessary ("the JDK permits ATOMIC_MOVE to replace an existing target on some providers") — an argument that applies verbatim to the two operations that skip it.

Fix: writeNew and claim take the same sidecar lock; one coherent destination-collision protocol rather than four ad-hoc ones. Preserve claim's existing loser classification (SourceMissing vs SourceNotRegular vs AlreadyClaimed) — the comment at :128-129 documents a deliberate race-tolerant reading that must survive.

Acceptance: proven by P8.B3's separate-JVM tests, not by same-JVM fibers.
set.title: P8.C1: One destination-collision protocol for writeNew and claim
